A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, including Sections 1–5 and Appendices A–H. Full text and visual comparison supports reliable assessment; pages 11–45 are identical in text and rendered appearance.

before.justification: v2 reports original unlearning experiments, including benchmark performance, membership inference attacks, ablations and supplementary evaluations in Section 4 and Appendices E–H.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the main benchmark comparisons and all appendix experiments and visualizations.

M1.justification: Sections 2–3 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same SAM/NegGrad updates, parameter masking and Sharp MinMax procedure. No method component or objective changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-100, ImageNet-1K, CIFAR-10 and Tiny-ImageNet, retaining the same memorization-based, random-forget and corrupted-image scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments, including NegGrad, RL, SalUn, L1-Sparse, SCRUB and their optimizer variants. Appendix G.6 retains the same MSAM comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendices E–G retain identical forget-set selection, preprocessing, model configurations, training budgets, hyperparameters, evaluation metrics and testing procedures.

E4.justification: The retain-weight sensitivity analysis, mask-cutoff ablation, corruption tests, relearning attacks, entanglement analysis and loss-landscape visualizations are all retained without revision.

E5.justification: Appendix F.1 retains three runs with different seeds, Table 8 retains its mean-plus/minus-sigma reporting, and Figures 4–5 retain intervals labeled 95% confidence intervals. KLoM estimation information is also unchanged.

E6.justification: Matched numerical entries and plotted findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices, including benchmark, privacy, robustness, runtime and KLoM results. Table 4 moves without changing its values.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, lemmas, theorems, corollary and Appendix D proofs are unchanged. Main-text equations cross different page boundaries without mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same scientific claims about SAM under unlearning, the retain–forget tradeoff and Sharp MinMax. The added code-availability sentence does not change these contributions.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning controlled overfitting, geometric properties and dataset-specific behavior are unchanged, as are the applicability qualifications and limitations in Appendix B.3.

D1.justification: v2 promises a future code release in Appendix B.1. v3 adds a direct link to the authors' sharp-unlearn repository in the abstract, while retaining that older promise. Implementation details and settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including the identical reference list and related-work discussion in Appendix A.

P1.justification: v3 adds one code-availability sentence to the abstract and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The scientific prose, terminology and section order otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added abstract line causes limited main-text reflow, including relocating Table 4 from page 8 to page 9. Figure graphics, table structures, captions and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new repository link provides a concrete code-access reference absent from v2, modestly improving reproducibility documentation. Scientific content remains unchanged. The benefit is limited by Appendix B.1's unrevised release promise; the supplied PDFs do not establish the repository's contents or usability.
